questions.q: In John 14:26, Jesus spoke of the Holy Spirit as the "Helper" or "Comforter." What did He say the Holy Spirit would specifically do for the disciples?
options: Destroy the Roman Empire to establish Israel
Teach them all things and bring to remembrance all He had said to them
Give them infinite wealth to spread the gospel
Turn all their enemies into pillars of salt
questions.explain: Jesus comforted them by saying: "But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you."

questions.q: Before ascending to heaven (Acts 1:4-5), Jesus gave the apostles a strict instruction regarding their location. He commanded them not to depart from ________, but to wait for the promise of the Father.
options: Jericho
Galilee
Jerusalem
Bethlehem
questions.explain: Acts 1:4 states: "And while staying with them he ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father... for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit."

questions.q: On which prominent Jewish festival did the Holy Spirit dramatically descend upon the apostles gathered in the upper room?
options: The Feast of Tabernacles
The Day of Pentecost
The Day of Atonement
The Feast of Trumpets
questions.explain: Acts 2:1 confirms this exact timing: "When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all together in one place."

questions.q: When the Holy Spirit descended on the believers in Acts 2, two dramatic physical signs accompanied His arrival. One was a sound like a mighty rushing wind. What was the other?
options: An earthquake that shook the foundations of the house
Divided tongues as of fire resting on each of them
A thick cloud of white smoke filling the room
A rain shower inside the upper room
questions.explain: Acts 2:2-3 describes the event: "And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like a mighty rushing wind... And divided tongues as of fire appeared to them and rested on each one of them."

questions.q: Following the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost, Peter delivered a powerful sermon. What was the tremendous numerical effect of this first speech on the church? (Acts 2:41)
options: About a hundred people were baptized.
About three thousand souls were added to their number that day.
Exactly twelve new disciples joined them.
Over ten thousand people were instantly converted.
questions.explain: The text states: "So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls."
